name: japan-macro-data-fetcher
what_it_holds: Python tool to fetch key Japanese macro indicators (consumption, CPI) via the e-Stat API, with interactive table search, 'smart table recommendation', and auto-cleaning CSV export. General e-Stat querying tool, not limited to headline CPI.
why_useful: A second, more generic e-Stat client (vs. the CPI-specific tracker above) that could be pointed at Japan's detailed CPI item tables to pull the lodging/hotel-charges component and consumption series relevant to APAC nights/ADR work.
themes: Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation
why_all: A second, more generic e-Stat client (vs. the CPI-specific tracker above) that could be pointed at Japan's detailed CPI item tables to pull the lodging/hotel-charges component and consumption series relevant to APAC nights/ADR work.

name: MyEuroStatApp
what_it_holds: Open-source Kotlin Multiplatform mobile/desktop client for the public Eurostat API, with a dedicated tourism module alongside economy, population, environment, trade, social, and science modules. AGPL-3.0 licensed, updated 4 Sep 2026 (actively maintained). No data committed; it is a generic Eurostat-API pull client.
why_useful: Lower priority than pandaSDMX/eurostat-R for programmatic pulls, but confirms an actively updated (2026-09-04) general Eurostat client exists if a GUI-based check of HICP accommodation figures is ever wanted.
themes: Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation
Electricity, water and waste data as occupancy proxies (smart-meter open data, tourist-area utility consumption), and mobile-phone tourism statistics (Eurostat MNO experimental)
why_all: Lower priority than pandaSDMX/eurostat-R for programmatic pulls, but confirms an actively updated (2026-09-04) general Eurostat client exists if a GUI-based check of HICP accommodation figures is ever wanted.

A maintained, general-purpose Eurostat API client that already has a tourism module could be adapted to pull MNO-derived experimental tourism tables (or the tour_ce_omr series we already hold) programmatically, though it duplicates a pull mechanism rather than adding new data.

name: Scraper_HICP_2
what_it_holds: Script for automated retrieval of Eurozone HICP data excluding tobacco through the Eurostat API (a specific headline aggregate, not confirmed to isolate the accommodation-services sub-index, but built on the same Eurostat API access pattern that could be redirected to the accommodation COICOP code).
why_useful: One more working example of a minimal, current Eurostat-API pull script; marginal on its own (headline ex-tobacco index, not accommodation-specific) but low-effort to verify/adapt.
themes: Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation
why_all: One more working example of a minimal, current Eurostat-API pull script; marginal on its own (headline ex-tobacco index, not accommodation-specific) but low-effort to verify/adapt.

name: greek-holidays-income
what_it_holds: Analysis of Greek household affordability of a week's holiday, built on Eurostat and Greek statistical authority (ELSTAT) data in Python — likely pulls Eurostat HICP/holiday-package price series plus income data for Greece specifically.
why_useful: A country-specific (Greece/Southern Europe) accommodation/holiday-price analysis that could surface a Greek CPI-accommodation or package-holiday price series not otherwise on our radar; EMEA/Southern-Europe granularity is thin in what we currently hold.
themes: Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation
why_all: A country-specific (Greece/Southern Europe) accommodation/holiday-price analysis that could surface a Greek CPI-accommodation or package-holiday price series not otherwise on our radar; EMEA/Southern-Europe granularity is thin in what we currently hold.

name: cpi-us
what_it_holds: Frictionless-Data/datahub.io core dataset: US CPI-U all-items index, monthly, January 1913-present, columns Date/CPI/Inflation MoM%, base 1982-84=100, sourced from the BLS API with GitHub Actions auto-monthly updates; processed CSV lands in `data/` after the build script runs.
why_useful: This is the ALL-ITEMS headline CPI-U, not the lodging-away-from-home sub-index, so it does not fill the specific gap on its own — flagged mainly as a clean, automatically-updated, long-history (1913+) CPI mirror pattern that could be forked/adapted to pull the CUUR0000SEHB lodging series instead of headline CPI.
license: PDDL/permissive (typical for datahub.io core datasets, not directly confirmed here)
size_hint: single CSV, small (a few thousand rows)
duplicate_of_holding: We already hold BLS CPI via FRED; this is headline CPI-U only, not the lodging component
themes: Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation
why_all: This is the ALL-ITEMS headline CPI-U, not the lodging-away-from-home sub-index, so it does not fill the specific gap on its own — flagged mainly as a clean, automatically-updated, long-history (1913+) CPI mirror pattern that could be forked/adapted to pull the CUUR0000SEHB lodging series instead of headline CPI.
